verdicts.tldr: the NewBanker parameter list offers BankerTypeReadonly as a value of bt, but NewBanker panics on that value
verdicts.details: At head docs/resources/gno-stdlibs.md:752-753 the rewritten header `- `bt` **BankerType** - type of Banker to get:` is followed by `- `BankerTypeReadonly` - read-only access to coin balances`, and 753 is unchanged but the branch rewrote the line that scopes the whole sub-list to the `bt` argument (base read `- `BankerType` - type of Banker to get:`). gnovm/stdlibs/chain/banker/banker.gno:117-120 rejects it: `func NewBanker(bt BankerType, rlm realm) Banker { if bt == BankerTypeReadonly { panic("use NewReadonlyBanker for BankerTypeReadonly") }`, so a reader who copies the documented call `banker.NewBanker(banker.BankerTypeReadonly, cur)` gets a panic; `NewReadonlyBanker` is named nowhere in the page. The panic predates the branch (identical at the merge base), so the branch did not invent the stale entry but did re-confirm it by rewriting the list header and adding the signature. Fix: drop the `BankerTypeReadonly` sub-bullet from NewBanker's parameters and add a sentence pointing at `banker.NewReadonlyBanker()` for readonly access.
verdicts.evidence: head docs/resources/gno-stdlibs.md:752 `- `bt` **BankerType** - type of Banker to get:` and :753 `    - `BankerTypeReadonly` - read-only access to coin balances`; head gnovm/stdlibs/chain/banker/banker.gno:118-120 `if bt == BankerTypeReadonly { panic("use NewReadonlyBanker for BankerTypeReadonly") }`; grep of the head page for `NewReadonlyBanker` returns no match (only lines 122, 732, 753 mention BankerTypeReadonly).
verdicts.angle: docs claim vs source: a parameter list that names a value the function refuses
verdicts.verify_by: sed -n '747,757p' docs/resources/gno-stdlibs.md and sed -n '104,124p' gnovm/stdlibs/chain/banker/banker.gno at head 7f309e625
